chunks: Yūnus, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning His, Exalted is He, saying:

He said: “Their iḥṣān is when intercourse has taken place with them.” He said: I said: “What do you think—if intercourse has not taken place with them and they commit an offense, what ḥadd is upon them?” He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أُحْصِنَّ: they are made muḥṣanāt, meaning they attain protected marital status
key_terms.إِحْصَانُهُنَّ: their iḥṣān, namely the legal state of marital protection in this context
key_terms.دُخِلَ بِهِنَّ: intercourse has taken place with them; the marriage has been consummated

ai.seo_question: What does «فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ» mean in relation to the ḥadd ruling for a married slave-woman?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase «فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ» as referring to women whose marriage has been consummated. It further indicates that consummation is the defining factor for iḥṣān in this legal context, which affects the application of the prescribed ḥadd.
